title: Panama in 1855
subtitle: An Account of the Panama Rail-Road, of the Cities of Panama and Aspinwall, with Sketches of Life and Character on the Isthmus
summary: Robert Tomes (1817–1882), an American physician and writer, went to the Isthmus of Panama in February 1855 as one of the guests of the Panama Rail-Road Company when its line from Aspinwall on the Atlantic to Panama on the Pacific was opened. He describes the voyage from New York, the new town of Aspinwall, the ride across the isthmus by rail, and the railway’s building, cost, and prospects, and then the old city of Panama, the island of Taboga, and an excursion to the Pearl Islands. He writes with humour about his fellow travellers, hotels, churches, officials, and the people of the isthmus. The book has a map of the railway and a few engravings.
